Your Future Team
The Office of the CMO is looking for an intern to help build the OCMO Insight Engine—an AI-powered solution that turns marketing performance data into concise, decision-ready insights for senior leaders.

In this role, you’ll use Atlassian tools, Rovo, and responsible AI practices to develop agents that analyze monthly OKR results, business reviews, and historical trends. The solution will help identify meaningful changes, surface areas requiring marketing leadership attention, and produce an executive report that highlights the decisions that matter most.

This is a hands-on opportunity to work at the intersection of artificial intelligence, business operations, data storytelling, and executive communications.

Responsibilities
Partner with the Office of the CMO to understand how marketing business reviews (and selected reports) are prepared and used.

  • Design and build Rovo-based agents that:

    • Ingest current- and prior-month Atlassian Goals scores and owner commentary.

    • Detect significant changes in key results and overall progress month over month.

    • Draft concise executive-summary bullets explaining the likely drivers of those changes.

    • Flag key results scoring low and generate questions for leadership follow-up.

    • Rebuild a month-over-month trend view without relying on a single reporting surface.

    • Produce a one-screen CMO pre-read (or dashboard) that distills multiple objectives and key results into the most important decision points.

  • Delivered a self-rebuilding month-over-month trend view.

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. Every product decision we make directly impacts the millions of Internet properties (powering websites, remote teams, APIs, and mobile apps) running on our global network. Cloudflare's network is one of the largest in the world, spanning over 330 cities in more than 125 countries, and operating within 50 milliseconds of 95% of the Internet-connected population globally (for context, the blink of an eye is 300 to 400 milliseconds!). We are passionate about making the Internet more secure, reliable, and faster for everyone.

Cloudflare’s Product Management team defines the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the features that power this massive global footprint. Product Managers bridge the gap between user needs, technical feasibility, and business impact by working directly with engineering, design, sales, and marketing to solve complex problems at scale. Team
Reality Labs Devices designs, builds, and ships Meta's consumer hardware, including AI glasses, Meta Quest, and the AR/VR devices on our roadmap. Hardware engineering, program management, manufacturing operations, supply chain, and logistics all sit in one organization, working the same product roadmap. A product passes through all of it, from prototype builds through mass production to customers in markets around the world, and it stays our responsibility from launch through end of life.

The Devices Product Engineering Operations team runs the operational backbone for those programs. We own the processes, systems, and reporting that connect engineering execution to business outcomes, partnering across hardware engineering, program management, finance, sourcing, and operations.

Role
As a TPM intern you will own a scoped workstream on a live program, sitting at the intersection of engineering execution and business outcomes. You will build schedules, track dependencies and risks, escalate blockers early, and translate hardware development and manufacturing detail into cost, schedule, and resourcing implications for both technical and business audiences.

You will work directly with hardware engineers, technical and operations program managers, finance and sourcing partners, and functional leads, building real fluency in both how consumer hardware gets built and how it gets funded, sourced, and shipped. Most projects take a recurring operations problem and solve it with Meta's internal AI tools and data platforms. You will be paired with a mentor and present your results to leadership at the end of the internship.

Projects are set closer to the start date based on where the business is. Examples of the kind of work you might do:
Trace how a change at one point in the supply chain, such as a supplier commit shortfall or a demand swing, moves through to factory output, distribution center inventory, and channel availability, and build a tool that sizes the impact and lays out the options.
Build a cost model for a part of unit cost that is hard to see today, such as logistics or post-sale support, and surface specific opportunities to reduce it.
Reconcile a costed bill of materials across procurement, product records, and manufacturing partners, and make that reconciliation repeatable.
Design workflow automation that eliminates manual handoffs and status-chasing, with proactive notification logic that surfaces exceptions before they hit program schedules.
Build a view that pulls status, risks, and metrics from every in-market program into one place and finds the patterns no single program can see.
Turn an operating playbook, such as how we qualify a change or launch a new market, into a structured process anyone on the team can run.

SPRING 2027 BUSINESS OPERATIONS INTERNSHIP/CO-OP

SpaceXSI seeks extraordinary students to join us for Spring 2027 business operations roles.   • Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s degree or graduate program
  • 3+ months experience in corporate and business functions (data analysis, finance, human resources, IT, government affairs, legal, advertising, and sales is applicable)

  • GPA of 3.5 or above
  • Strong interpersonal skills (examples: leading a student organization or working successfully in teams)
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail
  • Ability to work cross-functionally with different groups and teams
  • Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements
  • Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Able to work full time, onsite for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning in January or March 2027

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:
